hints: Look closely at the POS structure on the left. Which fatty acid chain has a C=C double bond, and which two chains have only single C-C bonds?
Compare the lengths of the top chain (P) and bottom chain (S) in POS. Count how many carbons longer S is than P, then use that to compare SOS with POP.
walkthrough:
**Spot saturated vs unsaturated**

First, be a detective with the diagram. The middle chain (O, oleic acid) clearly shows a C=C double bond in the middle. That means it is unsaturated.

The top chain (P, palmitic acid) and bottom chain (S, stearic acid) have only single bonds between carbons, with maximum H atoms. That means they are both saturated.

**Compare chain lengths for P and S**

Now count carbons. Palmitic acid (P) is a 16-carbon fatty acid. Stearic acid (S) is an 18-carbon fatty acid. Oleic acid (O) is also 18-carbon but unsaturated.

You can see this in the diagram: the S chain is two carbons longer than the P chain. So: S = P + 2 carbons.

**Compare the whole triglycerides**

Each triglyceride is glycerol (3 carbons, same in all) + 3 fatty acids. So any difference comes only from the fatty acids.

POP = P + O + P
SOS = S + O + S

Replace each S with (P + 2): SOS has two S chains instead of two P chains, so it has 2 + 2 = 4 more carbons in total than POP.

options.A: POP is P + O + P. Only O is unsaturated, while both P chains are saturated. So it has one unsaturated fatty acid, not two.
options.B: POS is P + O + S and POP is P + O + P. Since S is two carbons longer than P, POS has two MORE carbons than POP, not two less.
options.C: SOS has two S chains where POP has two P chains. Each S is 2 carbons longer than each P, so 2 x 2 = 4 more carbon atoms in total. This is correct.
options.D: SOS does contain two saturated fatty acids (the two S chains), but they are joined to glycerol by ester bonds formed by condensation, not joined by hydrolysis. Hydrolysis breaks them apart.
